newsitem.title: KENYA: Spanish aid worker reports mayhem in east Zaire.
newsitem.headline: Spanish aid worker reports mayhem in east Zaire.

text.p: A Spanish aid worker on Friday reported virtual mayhem in eastern Zaire where at least 175,000 refugees were on the move through barren, rough country in one area and armed groups rampaged through villages and camps.

The aid worker, who escaped Zaire on Wednesday, told a meeting at the U.N. Department of Humanitarian Affairs (DHA) in Nairobi that refugees were dying in barren volcanic lava fields west of their camps.
DHA officials quoted him as saying refugees broke into all the warehouses in Katale and Kahindo camps, with a combined population of 314,000, and stripped them bare as they moved out last week.
He said some 3,000 tonnes of food were looted from the largest U.N. World Food Programme store in the area of Kahindo camp, north of the border city of Goma seized by rebels last week.
Three or four big columns of refugees then left the camps, the largest heading west into a wide expanse of volcanic lava fields which emit gases and where there is no food or water.

The Spaniard, who works for Medecins du Monde (MDM-Doctors of the World), said other refugees headed into surrounding bush and forest. "We were amazed to see some of them climb up the mountains. We could see the camp fires at night," he added.
He said some local aid agency workers joined the huge columns of fleeing refugees but radio signals from them died last week.
He said competing armed groups of Zairean soldiers from various army units, exiled Rwandan Hutu militiamen and Rwandan Hutu refugees were rampaging in the region, looting camps and Zairean villages.
He said former Rwandan soldiers twice threatened to execute him and a contingent of Zairean troops paid by the U.N. refugee agency to guard the refugee camps and aid operations also fled.
The aid worker walked barefoot for 25 km (16 miles) to escape and reported deserted villages on a 35-km (22-mile) stretch of road between Rutshuru north of Goma and the Ugandan border.

At the same meeting, an aid worker for Action for Churches Together (ACT) reported a survey by plane this week showed a large concentration of people in the jungle between the Zairean towns of Hombo and Walikale.

He said the mixture of Rwandan refugees and displaced Zaireans had survived in the jungle for about three weeks and were "in very bad condition". He said they were very tense and were robbing each other.

ACT said empty villages, schools and markets and fields with no one working in them were visible and only one car was seen on a 200-km (125-mile) stretch of road to Lubutu, 300 km (185 miles) northwest of Goma.

It is unclear how many refugees remain in Mugunga camp west of the city of Goma. Before heavy fighting for Goma last week it was the largest refugee camp in the world, crammed with some 400,000 people.

A three-week rebel advance from the south of eastern Zaire has uprooted tens of thousands of Zaireans and large numbers of the 1.1 million Rwandan refugees and 200,000 Burundian refugees in the region.

Aid agencies are struggling to plan how to reach refugees but many of them have left rebel-controlled areas and dispersed to the west rather than follow U.N. suggestions that they head east back to Rwanda.
